dataModelChanges.details: Replace the two native <select> controls (#insrc-active, #insrc-history) with <button> triggers (aria-haspopup='menu', aria-expanded toggled) plus custom div menus, and cache the list entries client-side as histEntries (ChatSummary[]) and actEntries (ActiveChatEntry[]) plus the selected-id strings histSel and actSel. The trigger renders from selected-id membership: histChatFor(id) returns the histEntries entry when id is present, else undefined; activeChatFor(id) returns the actEntries entry when id is present, else undefined. An unsaved draft has no persisted record, so it is absent from BOTH lists (activeChats enumerates persisted records with status, and history holds only saved chats); membership-driven rendering therefore clears both selections and shows the empty placeholders ('no active work' / 'new…') until the draft's first save enters it into history.

Each open row is built through mitem with sel = (chat.id === selectedId), label = chat.title and icon = pico(chat.provider), so the real inline provider SVG renders per row — the gap the native option background-image cannot close. Active rows additionally render a status dot coloured through the DOT map {waiting-input:'red', working:'yellow', done:'green'}; the active trigger still shows the highest-ranked status.

Activation becomes a WRITER, and both selected ids are reconciled to the host-confirmed current session (cur) on EVERY host message: (1) on activating chat B — an active row or a persisted history row — the click/Enter handler writes actSel = histSel = B optimistically and re-renders both triggers before posting open-chat {chatId: B}, so the triggers flip immediately; activating the history 'new…' row posts new-chat {provider: curProv} unchanged (no optimistic write — there is no chat yet). (2) on session-restored, cur = m.sessionId, then reconcile BOTH selections and re-render in the order actSel then histSel: actSel = cur when cur is present in actEntries, else cleared ('no active work'); histSel = cur when cur is present in histEntries, else cleared ('new…'). (3) on history-list AND on active-list, re-settle BOTH selections against cur the same way (actSel = cur when present in actEntries else clear; histSel = cur when present in histEntries else clear): a rejected open-chat arrives as history-list alone (no session-restored, no active-list), so the history-list handler reconciles both selections — the active trigger snaps back to the confirmed session even when the stale id B remains in the cached actEntries and no active-list arrives. (4) the run-config branch (2484) no longer paints the chat triggers from curProv — it only updates curProv and the run-config button labels; paintSel/paintOpt/picoUrl are removed with the native chat selects.

Keyboard and focus lifecycle (replaces the native selects' built-in interaction). The two triggers are <button> elements with aria-haspopup='menu'; Enter/Space on a focused trigger toggles its menu (the same keydown pattern as the existing '>' send button, line 2510), and aria-expanded reflects the open state. Each menu is a role='menu' panel whose rows are mitem's role='menuitem' divs; the chat-menu builder assigns a roving tabindex (the focused row tabindex=0, the others -1) and tracks the focused index in a JS variable the keydown handler reads (mitem's signature and structure are unchanged, so the run-config callers are untouched). On open, focus moves to the selected row when one exists, else to the first enabled row; an empty menu shows a single disabled placeholder row and focus stays on the trigger. Arrow Up/Down move the focused row with wrap-around, Home/End jump to first/last, Enter/Space activate the focused row (the same handler as click), Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger, Tab closes the menu and moves focus onward, and an outside click closes the menu — the existing document click + Escape closePops pattern (lines 2394-2395) is extended to cover the two chat menus. On activation the menu closes and focus returns to its trigger. Opening one chat menu closes the other chat menu and the run-config provider/effort popups.

errorCases.response: render the row without an icon and fall back to the chat title alone; the trigger shows the title without an icon

errorCases.userImpact: the chat is still listed and selectable; only the icon is missing for that provider

errorCases.scenario: the selected id (actSel/histSel) points at a chat the host no longer recognises (rejected open-chat or removed between renders)
errorCases.detection: an open-chat was rejected or the selected chat was removed: the host answers with history-list alone (no session-restored, no active-list) and cur is unchanged; histChatFor(id) and activeChatFor(id) return undefined for the optimistic id (it is neither in histEntries/actEntries nor the confirmed current cur)
errorCases.response: the history-list handler re-settles BOTH actSel and histSel against cur (actSel = cur when present in actEntries else clear; histSel = cur when present in histEntries else clear), so both triggers return to the confirmed session — the active trigger clears the stale id even though it may remain in the cached actEntries and no active-list arrives
errorCases.userImpact: both triggers snap back to the confirmed session on the history-list response alone — no crash and no stuck stale icon

errorCases.scenario: the session-restored message arrives before the list entries have been cached
errorCases.detection: session-restored arrives before history-list / active-list have cached histEntries / actEntries
errorCases.response: defer reconciliation to the next history-list / active-list render: keep the raw restored id (cur) and re-run the membership check once histEntries/actEntries are populated (histSel then actSel)
errorCases.userImpact: the triggers may briefly read the empty placeholder, then flip to the restored chat when the lists arrive

invariantsToPreserve.text: activating an active row posts open-chat with its chatId; activating a persisted history row posts open-chat with its chatId; activating the history 'new…' row posts new-chat with the current provider — each message is unchanged, and a persisted history row is never routed through new-chat regardless of active-list membership.

mitem's first parameter stays a SELECTED boolean and its role=menuitem / .pico / .chk / .lbl structure is unchanged, so the run-config renderProvPane/renderModelPane callers are untouched; the chat-menu builder sets tabindex on the returned rows, not mitem itself.
the per-row provider mark is the real inline SVG from pico(provider), not a text glyph or an option background-image (which the native popup cannot render).
the DOT status-colour mapping {waiting-input:'red', working:'yellow', done:'green'} and the highest-ranked aggregate status on the active trigger are preserved.
an unsaved draft has no persisted record and is therefore absent from both actEntries and histEntries; it renders the empty placeholders (never a synthesized row) and is never an activation route.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API is affected — the change is internal webview chrome. The open-chat / new-chat IPC messages and the ChatSummary/ActiveChatEntry payloads are unchanged, so no host or IPC contract needs to stay backward compatible. Steps 1-5 are one atomic webview change and roll back together: changing the markup alone leaves the existing .options/.value/change handlers incompatible with the replacement buttons.

migrationSteps.action: Replace the two native <select> controls (#insrc-active, #insrc-history) with button triggers plus custom div menus, and cache the list entries client-side as histEntries/actEntries plus the selected-id strings histSel/actSel.
Render each open row through mitem with icon = pico(chat.provider) and sel = (chat.id === selectedId); add the DOT-coloured status dot to active rows.
Change the activation handlers (active and history) to WRITE actSel/histSel optimistically and re-render the triggers before posting open-chat / new-chat.

Reconcile actSel then histSel on session-restored, and re-settle both selections on history-list / active-list (recovering a rejected open-chat); remove paintSel/paintOpt/picoUrl with the native chat selects.
Wire the keyboard/focus/aria lifecycle for both menus (roving focus, Enter/Space activation, Escape/Tab/outside-click dismissal, popup coordination).

migration.stateAfter: Both controls are button triggers plus custom div menus whose rows render the real inline provider icon via mitem's icon param (pico(chat.provider)) and, for active rows, a DOT-coloured status dot, with a keyboard/focus lifecycle (roving focus, Escape/Tab/outside-click dismissal, popup coordination). The active trigger reads 'no active work' when no id is selected (membership-driven rendering); activation writes actSel/histSel optimistically and re-renders the triggers before posting the unchanged messages; session-restored reconciles actSel then histSel against the restored session and cached entries, and history-list/active-list re-settle the selections to the confirmed current session (recovering a rejected open-chat).
migration.stateBefore: The dev-chat header renders two native <select> controls — #insrc-active with an 'active…' empty placeholder and #insrc-history with a 'new…' empty placeholder. Per-chat provider marks are painted as option background-images via paintOpt/paintSel/picoUrl, which native select popups cannot render, and activation reads act.value/hs.value through change listeners to post open-chat / open-chat+new-chat.

summary.prose: The dev-chat header's two dropdowns — history and active chats — will each show the provider icon (Claude, Codex or Vibe) next to every chat, so a user can tell at a glance which provider a chat is running on. When no chat is active, the active-chat dropdown reads 'no active work' instead of the current 'active…' placeholder. The change is contained to the chat webview: the native <select> controls are replaced with custom menus so the real inline provider icon can render per row, which the native popup cannot.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test (tsx) with the chat-panel fake-DOM harness for pure logic; real-browser (headless Chrome screenshot) for interaction. Fake-DOM limitations and how each is handled: (1) innerHTML is not parsed into descendants, so icon tests assert the returned row's innerHTML CONTAINS the pico(chat.provider) SVG string (a string match), not a .pico descendant read; (2) native focus is inert, so the menu tracks its focused index in a JS variable and unit tests assert that index's transitions by invoking the keydown handler with synthetic events — actual focus movement, document-level outside-click propagation and bubbling are verified in the real browser, not fake-DOM; (3) document listeners are not dispatched in fake-DOM, so dismissal tests invoke the close handler directly, and real-browser smoke verifies actual outside-click.

testLevels.purpose: Prove the pure logic against the fake-DOM harness: the row innerHTML contains the real per-row provider SVG string, the empty active trigger reads 'no active work', activation writes the selected id optimistically, every host message (session-restored/history-list/active-list) reconciles BOTH selections against cur (including recovery from a rejected open-chat on a history-list-only response and the session-restored-before-list ordering), the persisted-history vs new-chat message split, unknown-provider fallback, and the menu keyboard/focus logic via the roving-focus index.

uxDefinition.narrative: Mock of the dev-chat header's two dropdowns. The header shows the two button triggers — #insrc-active reading 'no active work' and #insrc-history reading 'new…' — each opening an anchored menu shown directly below its trigger. Every chat row shows the ACTUAL provider icon (Claude, Codex or Vibe — the repo's own media/providers SVGs, inlined as data URIs so nothing is fetched) next to the chat title; active rows add a status dot coloured green/yellow/red for done/working/waiting-input. The empty states are called out at the bottom: with no selection the active trigger reads 'no active work' and the history trigger 'new…', with no icon.
